source_review.notes: Checked thirteen primary sources: current Apache Kafka introduction, design, record format, topic configuration, operations, and tiered-storage documentation; current Apache BookKeeper concepts/protocol; Apache Pulsar architecture, retention, and tiered-storage documentation; the current Apache Flink Kafka connector; and the original Raft paper. All cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Product-specific guarantees are attributed and not treated as universal log behavior.

evidence: Reviewed partition p/P, log start L_p, exclusive high H_p, bounded start/end S_p/E_p, next checkpoint C_p, and half-open interval notation.
Checked record identity, partition position, writer/leader epoch, committed/stable boundary, snapshot vector, and retention headroom remain distinct.
Checked MiB/TiB, seconds/days, physical copy count, percentage headroom, position span, and visible record counts use explicit units.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Offsets are consistently partition-scoped positions; no cross-partition arithmetic is presented as chronology or global identity.

evidence: Executed partition-log-snapshot with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced positional span 6, five physical records, one hole, final state A=v2/C=v1/X=v7, and checkpoints {0:5,1:4}.
Recomputed compact example spans 45+40=85 and retention gap [110,120) of ten positions; recomputed seven days at 50 MiB/s as approximately 28.84 TiB before copies/overhead.
Recomputed exercises: span 115, visible records 92, difference 23; 82,944,000 logical MiB and 268,738,560 physical MiB = 256.2890625 TiB.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable fixture demonstrates local interval, compaction-hole, tombstone, and checkpoint arithmetic only; it is not a broker or connector simulation.

evidence: Verified finite input is the union over frozen partitions of application-visible records in half-open [S_p,E_p) intervals with L_p<=S_p<=E_p<=H_p.
Checked H_p-C_p and E_p-S_p are positional spans, while compaction/control/transaction filtering can make readable cardinality smaller.
Verified capacity dimensions: MiB/s times seconds times headroom times physical copies times storage overhead yields provisioned MiB.
Reviewed next-unread convention: after incorporating offset o the next checkpoint is o+1, subject to coordinated state/effect durability.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Completeness is relative to frozen partition membership, interval bounds, and visibility; it is not a claim that retention/compaction preserved original history.

evidence: Reviewed empty partitions/intervals, start=end, start below L_p, end above H_p, compacted holes, sparse entries, control batches, pending/aborted transactions, and new/deleted partitions.

Reviewed producer timeout ambiguity, duplicate retries, sequence/epoch rollover, obsolete writers, divergent suffixes, replica/quorum loss, corrupt lengths/MACs, decompression expansion, and stale metadata.

Reviewed retention outrunning checkpoints, tombstone expiry, asynchronous compaction, partition-count/key-routing changes, old schemas, invalid timestamps, tier outage, and remote/local retention differences.
Reviewed cross-tenant/region access, credential rotation, revoked authorization, metrics leakage, deletion/holds, replay amplification, and disaster restoration.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Durability, readable visibility, replay completeness, processing effects, capacity, and governance can fail independently.

evidence: Traced producer serialization/routing through acknowledged append, replica commit, reader visibility, bounded interval, processing, next-position checkpoint, replay, and effects.
Checked cluster/topic/partition/incarnation/epoch/position identity and partition-local ordering remain stable across failover and replay.
Checked schema/key/partitioner/timestamp/transaction visibility are pinned in the source contract and bounded manifest.
Checked retention/compaction/tombstone/tier policies cover required start positions and all gap/corruption cases fail visibly rather than reset silently.
invariant_checking.notes: Broker durability protects source history only under its stated failures; checkpoint/effect protocols separately protect derived state.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from qualified source identity through record semantics, append guarantees, bounded intervals, retention validation, visibility, replay horizon, state coordination, observability, and lifecycle.
Checked the set-based bounded-input argument assigns every application-visible record in the manifest intervals once without inferring cardinality from offset span.
Checked leader/writer fencing and epoch qualification prevent obsolete histories from being mistaken for committed lineage under the source's protocol.
Reviewed counterexamples for global order, offset-as-ID/time/count, latest-as-complete, acknowledgement-as-exactly-once, compaction-as-history, reset-as-recovery, and tiering-as-backup.
proof_review.notes: The chapter distinguishes general log-source requirements from Kafka, BookKeeper, Pulsar, Flink, and Raft-specific mechanisms.

evidence: Audited uses of committed, acknowledged, durable, visible, ordered, idempotent, transactional, exact, bounded, complete, compacted, replicated, and replayable.
Confirmed every strong property is scoped to partition, visibility/isolation, configured acknowledgement/quorum, failure model, retention horizon, or processing protocol.
Confirmed product-specific current behavior is sourced and the Raft reference is labeled background rather than an assertion that all product logs use Raft.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No offset, broker commit, producer idempotence, compaction, or tiered-storage feature is mislabeled as universal end-to-end exactly-once behavior.

evidence: Reviewed measures for per-partition ingress, append latency/retry, epochs, replica health, start/high/stable/checkpoint positions, positional/time/byte lag, and replay headroom.
Reviewed segment/compaction/tombstone/tier, corruption/decode, transaction filtering, throttling, skew, reassignment, auth, and checkpoint-age evidence.
Confirmed no universal partition count, retention/tombstone horizon, replica/quorum configuration, segment size, batch size, lag threshold, tier policy, or reset behavior is prescribed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Operational choices require measured rates/tails, failure domains, engine versions, replay objectives, threat model, cost, and policy.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distributed logs as partition-scoped append sequences and durable input contracts spanning record/batch format, ordering domains, acknowledgement, replication/fencing, visibility, bounded snapshots, retention, compaction, schemas, timestamps, partition evolution, tiering, checkpoints, observability, and lifecycle.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed practical source manifests, next-offset convention, producer ambiguity/idempotence, committed isolation, retention headroom, tombstone rebuild safety, schema/key migrations, tiered reads, gap response, per-partition metrics, failure drills, authorization, and deletion. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from log identity and offsets through durability/visibility, finite snapshots, lifecycle transformations, processing integration, and validation. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover partition scope, checkpoints, lag holes, duplicate appends, capacity, retention gaps, tombstones, snapshot membership, transactions, and manifests.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Kafka, BookKeeper, Pulsar, or Flink maintainer, consensus/replicated-log researcher, streaming/runtime/storage/network/SRE practitioner, schema/data-governance or security/privacy specialist, records/legal authority, affected-tenant reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
